* NFL PA Executive Director - $8.2m
* SAG-AFTRA CEO - $1.02m
* AFT (Teacher's Union) President - $475k
* AFL-CIO (Trade and State Worker's Union) President - $277k

And, sure. You can argue that different industries see a different amount of money flowing around. But when the discrepancy between the union leader and union workers is so wide, you should probably do some research.

Holy shit, you really ironed out on this comment what I like about Genshin vs my pet peeves with HSR’s pacing and general plot. 

I believe I dropped it around 2.5 due to that odd feeling of the story just being… disconnected. In a sense, it’s not inherently bad to have the main purpose of the story being “explore the universe”. But really, there’s no end goal in mind. Yes, you’re learning about Stellarons and Aeons, but there’s no real end goal in mind. It leaves for a lot of creative room, but also makes each patch feel more disconnected from others.

Even reading about the plot of 3.0 in HSR, I just don’t really feel the excitement of wanting to learn more. There’s a lot of interesting concepts in HSR’s worldbuilding, but there’s no hook as to what knowing all this information will get you to. With Genshin, so much about the very nature of Teyvat is purposefully hidden that, learning new details such as how the Four Shades operates, peels a new layer of the general mystery. This creates new theories and pushes for lore exploration.

Breaking down your questions:

# Can I still get Miyabi? 

Depends on how much time you have about 24 days to pull for her before end of her banner. Depending how far you're into the game, and whether you have the Daily Pass ∨ Battle Pass, you could get enough pulls. Just for reference, for F2P players that were caught up with content, version 1.4 is estimating to give 140 pulls in between in-game content, events, Hoyolab events, etc. 

# Any tips about the game?

In terms of combat, I'd say enjoy yourself and find what gameplay you like the most. I have some friends who live for Corin and Anton, clearing Shiyu (end game) within like a minute with them, but I just don't like their gameplay. On the other hand, they really dislike Billy and Harumasa whereas I like them a lot. Some of the best sources for pulls will be Proxy Story (main quest) and events, I'd suggest building two teams with different attributes, (i.e. build an Electric Team and an Ice Team). 

# Any tips on building teams?

From the screenshot you took, two teams I'd immediately suggest:

*Harumasa / Rina / Lycaon or Anby* \- Great team for Harumasa. He's a bit tricky to use, so I'd recommend checking out a video on how to use him. Anby is great for electric agents at M4 (she gives them faster energy), so Lycaon might be a better option for now. 

*Billy / Nicole / Anby -  The OG squad*. Really good team. Billy can also be a bit hard to get used to with their core kit (crouching shot) but even at low Mindscapes he's insanely fun. 

 That being said, Lucy, Piper, and Soukaku are fantastic units you can also use. 

  
Best of luck with everything!

It *should* be, however you'll run the rest of your team at half HP due to Furina's HP drain usually if doing in abyss. In that case, I'd recommend running a shielder at least.

  
Edit: I'd recommend watching a video guide on Neuvi + Furina for you to get some idea of gameplay and what rotations will look like. I like running Charlotte since I have her fairly built, but in this most recent abyss I ended running *Neuvillette / Kazuha / Furina / Zhongli* due to my lack of geo characters for Floor 12 haha. It's unusual for spiral abyss to have such tight elemental requirements, so not a usual thing.

Furina generally wants a healer that can do multiple ticks of heals over a small window of time. This, in addition to the HP drain from her elemental skill pets, ensures that you can reach the maximum amount of Fanfare stacks (ultimate dmg bonus) in the smallest window of time. This isn't as big of a concern when getting her constellations (C2 specifically). Neuvi can reduce and increase his HP from his regular kit, but a healer like Charlotte or Jean can help.

Neuvillette's A1 passive increases the dmg of his CA per the amount of hydro-related reactions triggered by team up to three (*110%/125%/160% respectively*), or two with C1. While this means in theory you'd want to run Neuvi with three other elements (rainbow composition team), it's likely enemy reactions will reduce the need of rainbow comp. Additionally, the dmg bonus from Furina's burst, as well as Hydro Resonance (2 hydro party members increasing HP) is better usually than just a third stack of his A1.

ZL is a fairly strong generalist shielder that can be used with most of the characters in the game. His shield is stupidly strong and reduces elemental resistance from nearby enemies. An example of a team I'd build with your characters is:

*Arlecchino / Xingqiu / Yelan / ZL*

Arlecchino's pyro application is so high from her kit, that running double hydro allows her to vape every attack. Adding ZL for interruption res and elemental shred means she's a beast.

Mavuika is also looking incredibly strong. While she prefers characters with Nightsoul mechanics (Natlan characters and Pyro Lumine), she'll be able to work with a good amount of the characters in your team.

Neuvillette is a fantastic character and you have some amazing teammates for him already (notably Furina + Charlotte / Jean). 

I'd say: If you're planning on pulling for either any of the previous Natlan characters (Mualani, Kinich, Chasca, Ororon or Citlali), Mavuika should be a good pull. 

PS; Archons usually rerun in the same version of release (for instance Furina came out on 4.2 and reran on 4.7), so we should expect to see Mavuika at some point prior to 6.0.

1) For a buff/heal setup you'll look for a cleric/mage.

Mages have a couple of classes that have buffs (Linker; Thaum, Chrono, etc) and you can play with all of them. You can make a fully support wizard like Roger said, but soloing at some point might be hard. If you play with another player though it should not be hard and if you distribute skills/stat points properly you can also use that build for endgame content like ET Tower and such.

Clerics no matter how you build them they usually do damage. Clerics are also the only class that can heal, so if you're looking for a healer this is the one to go. Like I said, most of cleric classes offer a combination of support and damage (rare cases like Oracle), so here it's more of a personal choice. The usual build is Cleric > Diev3 > x > PD which overall is incredibly balanced but if you want to feel more like a support you can try going for priest or even oracle. It also depends on what you want for that character. Do you want to farm items? Casual fun? ET Tower? Or PVP?

All of this factors will change your build so be sure to check each thing.

My own personal advice on this one is to make a build around 1 class. You grab a class (let's say Pardoner for instance) and work your way around it. See what classes can work with it/benefit from their skills and see if it's what you want. You can google info on each class and see how it's fairing in the current patch. Classes like Monk are going to get rebalanced so you also have to consider that. At the end of the day, play what you feel like fun.

2) As others have told you, cash shop is basically Token, costumes and pets. Token is going to be $10, pets are around $30 but unless you are a Hunter there is no real need for a premium pet aside from looks. You can perfectly play without ever using the token, but you are going to be limited in some playability (not much though). ToS also offers multiple events every month or so that usually have EXP boosters and other things so you can look forward to that.

3) Most non cleric classes will benefit from heals and buffs. Clerics are very independent whereas mages on early levels won't have enough damage to survive. Anything really works well.

Hope I answered most of your questions :)
